Class TypeHierarchyWriter

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.inject.writer.TypeHierarchyWriter
@Internal public final class TypeHierarchyWriter extends Object
Writes the record of the generic hierarchy of a type, a TypeHierarchy found at run time with TypeHierarchies. See VisitorContext.importTypeHierarchy(ClassElement, Element...).

A record is a class with a constructor and nothing else, which passes the type, its variables, its direct super types and all its super types, built with the argument factories from class constants, to GeneratedTypeHierarchy. It is written into the package of the first originating element; only a type that is itself not public is recorded in its own package, the one package that can name it. A super type that the record cannot name, a class that is not public and of another package than the record or one whose arguments name such a class, is left out of the recorded closure with the types above it kept, and is recorded by the name of its class instead (TypeHierarchy.getOmittedSuperTypeNames()); a type whose variables are bounded by such a class is refused.

    • write

      public static void write(ClassElement type, String recordName, VisitorContext context, Element... originatingElements)
      Writes the record of a type. A type recorded several times into the same package is written once: a compiler that refuses a second write of the same class is taken at its word. A type recorded from several packages is written into each, see TypeHierarchies.find(String, ClassLoader).
      Parameters:
      type - The type
      recordName - The name of the record, from recordClassName(ClassElement, Element...)
      context - The visitor context
      originatingElements - The originating elements, at least one
